statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 19%, inside the low band, while Stress at 56% remains the elevated reading.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON on Tail 19%. The elevated component is Stress at 56%, carried by a long end at multi-decade yield extremes rather than by observed Nasdaq-100 trend persistence. The narrow danger window spans the 18:00Z Fed Hammack appearance through the 20:00Z cash close and into the 21:00Z CME weekly futures halt.
headline: Opening high retraced and the low bought back; two-way session keeps Tail in the low band while bond stress persists
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades 30,533.01, up 0.18% on the day, after reaching 30,649.20 early, handing the entire gain back to a 30,413.59 low and then recovering to mid-range. That completed round trip in both directions is the decisive structural observation: a directional attempt met supply, reverted, and the reversion itself was then bought. This is functioning mean reversion, the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension pattern that defines a pathological price path, so Tail moves down to 19% in the low band. VIX is 15.39, down 1.79% on the day and off its 15.94 session high, which corroborates the decay in realised volatility. The elevated reading remains in Stress. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.22%, up about five basis points and sitting at the top of its 5.17-5.23 daily range near multi-decade highs, after the 30-year reached 5.44% on Thursday, its highest since 2004. Crude is easing from elevated absolute levels, WTI near $94.04 (-0.60%) and Brent near $106.21, on reported US-Iran negotiations in New York over a phased agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and lift the port blockade; neither side has yet moved first, so the track remains unresolved. Today's U.S. data were soft but not disruptive: August durable goods orders were essentially flat, and final September Michigan sentiment revised up to 48.1 from 47.8 with one-year inflation expectations at 4.6%, the highest since June. Shared Finviz context collected at 14:12Z carries a partial status because its calendar and futures sections failed; the available breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections show latest-session semiconductor strength against mixed megacaps and split sectors. That context is delayed and non-real-time and is not used here as evidence of current Nasdaq-100 structure. Yields rising while crude eases and equities hold mid-range is a cross-asset conflict, which reduces directional conviction rather than establishing trend persistence. Dominant mode is mixed.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours held a narrow band: Tail between 17% and 24%, Stress between 54% and 59%, and Confidence between 86% and 88%, alternating between EA_ON and WATCH without ever approaching the block threshold. Dominant mode rotated through mixed, normal and three brief trend-up readings spanning the European morning. The 13:00Z slot has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable rather than filled in.
outlookSummary: The near-term path keeps Tail inside the low and watch bands, rising to 22% across the 18:00Z Fed Hammack appearance and the power hour into the Friday close, which together define the narrow danger window. The distinguishing feature of this horizon is that the CME weekly futures halt arrives at 21:00Z: the remaining eighteen hourly slots are halted, untradeable time in which no mean-reversion failure can develop, so Tail falls into the 9-11% range while Confidence decays from 75% to 55% as the last live observation ages. Stress stays elevated through the weekend and drifts up slightly at the end to reflect accumulated uncertainty from the unresolved US-Iran negotiation track and a long end at multi-decade yield extremes, both of which reprice at the Sunday reopen rather than inside any hour of this horizon.
